mechanism_narrative: A sustained month-over-month increase in non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) exceeding 0.5% signals strengthening labor market conditions that boost consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when PAYEMS increases by at least 0.5% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 7.0%, it indicates a tight labor market that accelerates consumer spending and corporate revenue growth, producing positive S&P 500 returns within 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when UNRATE falls below 7.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS ≤ 0.1%) and accelerating inflation (CPIAUCSL > 0.2% month-over-month) indicates accommodative policy amid inflationary pressures, which precedes positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: The joint condition of FEDFUNDS ≤ 0.1% and CPIAUCSL > 0.2% month-over-month fails to predict positive returns in more than 55% of cases over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS > 4.0% and rising for 3 months), S&P 500 experiences negative returns over 60 trading days due to reduced liquidity and higher discount rates for equity valuations.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.0% and rises for 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A month-over-month increase in housing starts (HOUST) exceeding 1.0% indicates robust consumer demand for housing, which correlates with broader economic expansion and positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when HOUST increases by at least 1.0% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) falls below 100.0, it signals manufacturing contraction that reduces corporate output and profits, leading to negative S&P 500 returns within 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when INDPRO falls below 100.0.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in real personal consumption (RSAFS) and GDP (GDPC1) exceeding 0.3% month-over-month indicates strong aggregate demand, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days through elevated corporate earnings.
failure_condition: The joint increase in RSAFS and GDPC1 fails to predict positive returns in more than 55% of cases over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion (UNRATE < 5.0% and PAYEMS growth > 0.4% month-over-month), rising non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) signal sustained economic momentum that drives positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods during late-cycle expansion when PAYEMS increases.
